applicability: The build reports a Mat, Acc, or Vec buffer overflow after reuse.
A cross-core mixed kernel reserves a pipe buffer whose slot depth is the real capacity consumer.
A hand-authored `pl.MemRef` must be isolated from all other allocations.
Choosing between deterministic PYPTO placement and capacity-aware DSA-RP placement.
directions: For deterministic default placement, use `MemoryPlanner.PYPTO` and inspect `memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt` when the default planner produces it; under PTOAS, compare exact compile candidate program instead.
For opt-in capacity-aware placement, compile with the documented `memory_planner=passes.MemoryPlanner.DSA_RP` option.

Use `pl.reserve_buffer(name='pipe', size=..., base=AUTO)` or the default `base=-1` to let the compiler pick a non-conflicting address, and `pl.import_peer_buffer(name=..., peer_func=...)` to share it.
When a cross-core reserve ring overflows Mat or Vec, reduce `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)` or shrink the tile that crosses the boundary.
Keep hand-authored reserve-buffer names distinct from generated pipe-buffer names; the capacity diagnostic only points to `pl.cross_core_slot` for an exact generated pipe name.
effects: PYPTO is deterministic and simple; DSA_RP can find a better capacity-fitting placement but is slower and depends on compatible ptoas synchronization.
A deeper cross-core ring lets the producer run ahead but consumes capacity in the consumer.
`reserve_buffer` makes a cross-core handoff explicit but hides its bytes from ordinary per-tile inspection.
invariants: PYPTO addresses are 32-byte aligned and deterministic by name order; views share their parent slot and keep relative offsets.
DSA_RP has a worst-case quadratic graph construction in the number of reusable buffers; it is opt-in and may emit `PH-DSA-001`.
PTOAS skips `AllocateMemoryAddr`; a memory map that depends on assigned addresses has nothing to draw.
The cross-core reserve ring lives in the consuming core's space; a Vec overflow in a function whose reserve is in Mat does not get the same remediation note.
A hand-authored buffer named like a generated pipe ring is not resizable by `pl.cross_core_slot`.
principle: Under `MemoryPlanner.PYPTO`, `AllocateMemoryAddr` collects unique MemRefs and assigns each memory space its own address range starting from zero unless a reserve buffer already reserved a leading window. Addresses are 32-byte aligned, MemRefs are sorted by name for determinism, and DDR is skipped. View MemRefs that share a base pointer are co-located in one slot sized by the largest member; each view keeps its relative byte offset, so a reshape of a slice that does not emit a subview still reads the correct offset. Under `MemoryPlanner.DSA_RP`, the pass builds an in-memory problem with hard lifetime interference, reserved ranges, semantic no-alias, target hazards, requested pipeline-stage separation, and hard arena capacity. Author-declared MemRefs are hard-separated. Soft unit-weight pairs model recognized cross-pipe WAR/WAW handoffs to discourage costly physical reuse. Canonical greedy tries offset zero, reserved-range ends, and aligned tops of placed neighbors, chooses the lowest incremental penalty and then the lowest address, and validates every placement. Pipeline intent is strict-then-soft: solve with all requested separations hard; if no fitting placement is found, relax only pipeline-intent pairs, add unit penalties, and solve again; if the relaxed placement overlaps a pair, emit `PH-DSA-001`. A no-fit result is a bounded-search failure, not an infeasibility certificate. DSA_RP depends on ptoas InsertSync recognizing physical range overlap across allocation roots; older ptoas releases are incompatible. `MemoryPlanner.PTOAS` skips address allocation and leaves placement to ptoas. `system.reserve_buffer(base=AUTO)` reserves a named leading window and is resolved to an explicit base; its bytes are counted in the high-water mark but are not a MemRef and are invisible in per-tile accounting. The cross-core pipe ring is `slot_size * slot_num` bytes in the consuming core's memory: Mat/L1 for V2C (`pl.aic_gather`), Vec/UB for C2V (`pl.aiv_shard`). `slot_size` is the full tile the consumer pops, and `slot_num` defaults to 2. Lower the depth with `optimizations=[pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)]` on the enclosing `pl.at(...)` or shrink the crossing tile. The ring depth is not auto-capped because that would turn a loud capacity error into a quiet throughput regression.
questions: Whether ptoas 0.60 in the local toolchain includes the cross-root physical-overlap analysis that DSA_RP requires was not tested.
risks: Reading a generic Mat overflow without noticing that most of it is reserved by a cross-core pipe floor.
Assuming `memory_planner=PTOAS` still produces assigned addresses and a drawable memory map.
Using an old ptoas whose InsertSync compares allocation-root identity rather than physical range with DSA_RP placements.
Believing a bounded DSA-RP no-fit result proves mathematical infeasibility.
summary: `AllocateMemoryAddr` gives concrete addresses to non-DDR MemRefs. PYPTO uses deterministic 32-byte-aligned sequential allocation per space; DSA_RP solves capacity-constrained placement with reuse penalties; PTOAS skips the pass. `pl.reserve_buffer` and cross-core pipe rings can dominate an overflow.
title: Address Allocation, DSA-RP, and Cross-Core Reserve Buffers
